sources.title: Jiří Lebl, Basic Analysis I: Introduction to Real Analysis, Volume I, version 6.3 (15 May 2026)
sources.locator: §3.6.1–3.6.2 (printed pp. 149–153): monotone-function conventions, one-sided limits, discontinuities, countability, and inverse continuity.
sources.source_kind_detail: Author-hosted complete 312-page undergraduate real-analysis textbook PDF; the cited monotone-function section was read in full.

read_evidence.extent: The complete version 6.3 PDF was retrieved and inspected. Section 3.6.1's full one-sided-limit proof (pp. 149–150), the countability corollary proof (pp. 150–151), and Section 3.6.2's inverse-continuity proof and its endpoint-of-image exercise boundary (pp. 151–153) were read. The book defines increasing as weakly increasing, opposite to this repository's convention; the source's weak use is translated to nondecreasing when comparing claims. The local items state and prove their own convention and endpoint cases.

contents.name: Definition 3.6.1: monotone and strictly monotone functions
contents.detail: The carrier keeps the repository convention: increasing/decreasing are strict and nondecreasing/nonincreasing are weak. Lebl uses increasing/decreasing for the weak notions; this vocabulary mismatch is explicitly noted and no source wording is copied without translation.

contents.name: Proposition 3.6.2: one-sided limits of monotone functions
contents.detail: The source proves one nondecreasing left-limit case and leaves symmetric cases as exercises. The local carrier proves all required directions, endpoint availability, extended-real limits, and order inequalities.

contents.name: Corollary 3.6.3: continuity and interval-valued image for a nonconstant monotone function
contents.detail: The source proves the interior converse and leaves interval endpoints as an exercise. The published local proof explicitly treats endpoints; the corollary is also used in the continuous-injection proof.

contents.name: Corollary 3.6.4: a monotone function has at most countably many discontinuities
contents.detail: The source assigns a rational to each discontinuity without fixing a uniform choice rule. The local proof uses one fixed rational enumeration and least indices, proving countability without a choice principle.

contents.name: Proposition 3.6.6: continuity of the inverse of a strictly monotone map on an interval
contents.detail: The source's increasing case leaves the missing-side cases as an exercise. The local proof supplies those cases and states the interval-image and singleton boundaries explicitly.

contents.name: Exercise 3.6.11: an increasing function discontinuous at every rational in [0,1]
contents.detail: The source gives only an enumeration-and-series hint. The local example supplies the complete bounded monotone construction, verifies every jump and continuity point, and extends it to all of R.

fetch_history.outcome: Complete author-hosted PDF retrieved; 312 pages; §3.6.1–3.6.2 inspected in full.

sources.title: Brian S. Thomson, Judith B. Bruckner, and Andrew M. Bruckner, Elementary Real Analysis, 2nd ed. (2008)
sources.locator: §5.9 (printed pp. 334–340) for monotone one-sided limits, jump discontinuities, countability and prescribed discontinuities; §9.8 (printed pp. 587–590) for continuity points of pointwise limits and the rational indicator example.
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete 1013-page second-edition textbook PDF, independently hosted by the University of South Carolina mathematics department.

read_evidence.extent: The complete PDF was retrieved and inspected. The full text of Theorems 5.60–5.61 and Example 5.62 (§5.9), Theorem 9.39 and Exercises 9.8.4 and 9.8.7 (§9.8), and the surrounding hypotheses were read. Theorem 5.61 relies on Exercises 5.9.12 and 4.6.10, Example 5.62 says the final continuity verification can be shown, and Theorem 9.39 cites Exercise 9.8.4; these are recorded as gaps in that source's local presentation. The local carriers provide complete proofs and do not use an exercise or sketch as a premise.

contents.name: Theorem 5.60: one-sided limits of monotone functions
contents.detail: The book reduces decreasing functions by negation and proves a sequence-based increasing case. The local proof instead derives both one-sided limits directly from supremum/infimum and states exactly when a side exists.

contents.name: Theorem 5.61: countability of discontinuities of a monotone function
contents.detail: The textbook's disjoint-jump-interval proof invokes Exercises 5.9.12 and 4.6.10. The local proof gives the omitted rational separation and a fixed least-index injection, so it is complete and choice-free.

contents.name: Example 5.62: a monotone function with a prescribed countable discontinuity set
contents.detail: The book presents a weighted-jump series and asserts the remaining continuity check. The local theorem handles empty, finite and countably infinite sets and proves convergence, boundedness, exact jumps and continuity away from the prescribed set.

contents.name: Theorem 9.39: a pointwise limit of continuous functions is continuous on a dense G-delta set
contents.detail: The source's full proof uses its earlier oscillation results and Exercise 9.8.4. The local proof supplies the closed oscillation superlevel result and interval Baire lemma as declared suppliers, then proves the dense G-delta conclusion.

contents.name: Exercise 9.8.7: the rational indicator is a pointwise limit of Baire-one functions but is not Baire one
contents.detail: The source states the challenge but does not solve it. The local example constructs finite-set indicators, their continuous approximants and the pointwise limit, then uses the continuity-point theorem to rule out Baire class one.

contents.name: Example 5.63: the Dirichlet function is discontinuous everywhere
contents.detail: The source records the limsup/liminf conclusion without a proof. The local theorem verifies the dense rational/irrational oscillation directly and also gives the full Thomae continuity set and oscillation formula.

sources.title: Ashutosh Kumar, MTH404: Analysis II, lecture notes, Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur
sources.locator: pp. 3–4, Baire Category Theorem; pp. 44–47, Baire class one continuity theorem, rational-indicator example and Baire hierarchy; pp. 48–50 for the adjacent Borel-function development.
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete 100-page university lecture-notes PDF; the cited proofs and surrounding definitions were inspected in full.

read_evidence.extent: The complete 100-page PDF was retrieved. The complete metric Baire category proof (pp. 3–4), Baire-one definition and continuity theorem (pp. 44–45), the pointwise-limit example and hierarchy (pp. 46–47), and the immediately following Borel-function section (pp. 48–50) were inspected. The notes prove the continuity theorem for R and use the complete-metric Baire theorem; the local carriers specialize to a closed interval and prove their countable constructions with the declared local lemma.

contents.name: Baire Category Theorem for complete metric spaces
contents.detail: The notes give the nested-ball proof. Their successive ball selections are not used by the local interval lemma, which uses a fixed rational enumeration and least-index choices to preserve the choice-free branch.

contents.name: Definition of Baire class one functions
contents.detail: The carrier uses the same pointwise limit of continuous functions convention on its explicitly stated domain.

contents.name: Points of continuity of Baire class one functions
contents.detail: The notes prove a real-line version using oscillation, closed Cauchy-tail sets and Baire category. The local proof retains its closed bounded interval domain and establishes the needed closedness and category inputs separately.

contents.name: Pointwise limits of Baire-one functions and the rational indicator
contents.detail: The notes state that finite rational-set indicators are Baire one and converge pointwise to the Dirichlet function. The local example supplies continuous approximants for those finite indicators and the full non-Baire-one argument.

contents.name: Baire hierarchy under pointwise limits
contents.detail: The local example proves the first strict hierarchy step directly; the notes' broader transfinite hierarchy is not imported as an axiom or proof premise.

contents.name: Borel functions and pointwise-limit closure
contents.reason: The adjacent Borel-measurability development concerns measurable preimages and hierarchy identification, neither of which is claimed by this pair; no Borel-function assertion is required for its continuity-set or Baire-one results.

contents.name: Cantor set as an uncountable null set
contents.detail: The notes state the Cantor-null result as a homework exercise; the local example imports the published Cantor-set proof and proves the Cantor-function image claim separately.

fetch_history.outcome: Complete 100-page lecture notes retrieved; pp. 3–4 and 44–50 inspected.

sources.title: Costas Efthimiou, Introduction to Functional Equations: Theory and Problem-Solving Strategies for Mathematical Competitions and Beyond (2011)
sources.locator: Chapter 11, pp. 150–159: Cauchy's additive functional equation, rational homogeneity, regularity criteria, and representation of non-linear additive solutions using a Hamel basis.
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete 362-page AMS textbook PDF; the complete cited chapter was read.

read_evidence.extent: The complete 362-page PDF was retrieved and Chapter 11 (pp. 150–159) was inspected. It develops rational homogeneity and the regularity consequences for additive functions and describes Hamel-basis representations. It does not prove existence of a Hamel basis; the local item obtains this from its explicit Axiom-of-Choice hypothesis and the published vector-space basis/Zorn suppliers.

contents.name: Rational homogeneity of additive functions
contents.detail: The local lemma gives the complete integer induction, negative-integer extension and rational division proof, rather than relying on a citation.

contents.name: Regularity conditions for Cauchy's functional equation
contents.detail: The source's regularity cases were checked against the local claims. The local proof derives all six conditions from its bounded-interval lemma and proves graph density by rational approximation in two independent directions.

contents.name: Hamel-basis representation of non-linear additive maps
contents.detail: The textbook assumes a Hamel basis exists and does not prove existence. The local proof declares Choice and derives existence through the current basis and Zorn suppliers before defining the coefficient functional.

contents.name: A non-linear additive function as a counterexample to the assertion that every additive function is linear
contents.detail: The local false-statement carrier gives the complete coefficient-map counterexample and explicitly preserves the Choice dependency.

fetch_history.outcome: Complete 362-page textbook retrieved; Chapter 11 inspected in full.
